doc.title: Dave Bailey and John McNeil Interview, 1959-10-25

title: Jimmy Jackson and the Gibson band; Doc Paulin
summary: Explanation of how the band was named Gibson after Jimmy Jackson (Alphonse Spears), and the dispute with Ernest Paulin.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Wait a minute, Jimmy Jackson what?

He's dead man, you know that? No. Sure, we played at the funeral. How long? It's going on six years now I believe it ought to be. The last time I saw his daughter at the hospital I believe she said it was going on five, and we're going on six now. Who's Gibson? That's the band I play in.
Yeah but who is Gibson that they named the band?
He just named the band that he named, the name Alphonse Spears, just named the band Gibson, the Gibson band.
Yeah but there's no such person as Gibson huh? No. Just made that up huh? Yeah. That's a kick. The Gibson band.

See because before it was named after Jackson, it was the Jackson band. You know what I'm saying? Yeah. Jimmy had a name behind him. His name was Alphonse Spears. I guess you didn't want to say Spears band, the name of the Egyptian band.
No. He knew how to play Snap a little bit. No he didn't play. He used to get the job. He'd get the job and he'd come in on it you know.
Did he ever work with you years ago or anything? No.

On Snap? No. In other words he just like a boss. He'd get the job. He'd be in the parade soon and have his little stick. Tell the boys what to play and all of them. And you know just like a grand marshal like that. He used to get all the jobs, get the wood. But one time he made a mess up at the Gordon District. He had two bands I was playing with playing too. I believe my band was in the front and he was behind. And he went and got that band. Called himself trying to do me a dirty trick. Something happened. I don't know if I was going to go rehearsing. I told him I couldn't make the rehearsals every Thursday like that. I'd be tired of working. You know what I mean? Hardest, other drum player in the band. And I was playing with a fella called Doc. Don't you know Doc?
Trumpet. Ernest Paulin is his name. He's calling him Doc.
Oh yeah, well I know Ernest Paulin. He lived right back here.

Back on Seventh Street out of the cemetery between Franklin and Liberty. Ernest Paulin is his name. They called him Doc. I was playing his band. And when he got through the Gondis, they weren't Jimmy Jackson's band no more. He was four, he signed a job for ten men and he brought nine. Well he got that money, man.

He wouldn't hire that band no more. Then after that he come back and he won't try to get me to play back in the band with him again. None of the drummers do nothing with me. I ain't bragging on myself, not in the brass band. Not if I see if they, it's all that long they don't try to buck in. If I see where they're going to buck in, then I'm going to cover them up.
